ownership_reason: Only the gold decides which entries of the column are visited: it counts the blocks, computes the start and height of each block and adds the scalar to each entry of each block. Hops 1, 3 and 4 pass the array and the scalar along, and hop 2 only returns early for an empty array. With the block count rounded down, a column shorter than one block has no block and keeps its entries, against the gold's javadoc ('Adds a scalar to each entry of a column'); no caller can make the gold visit those entries without replacing it or handing it a different array. The convention is pinned outside the gold: BlockFieldMatrix.createBlocksLayout and BlockRealMatrix.createBlocksLayout count blocks as (rows + BLOCK_SIZE - 1) / BLOCK_SIZE, the last block holding what remains (BlockFieldMatrix.blockHeight), with BlockFieldMatrixTest::testSeveralBlocks (37 x 41), BlockFieldMatrixTest::testDimensions (smaller than one block) and BlockRealMatrixTest::testSeveralBlocks passing; the step 'every entry receives d' is done by the intact OpenMapRealVector.mapAddToSelf and ArrayRealVector.mapSubtractToSelf, with SparseRealVectorTest::testMapFunctions passing.
